subject: Novel Method
source_sentence: We present a novel method that (1) exploits a pre-trained neural language model to obtain contextualised representations for every occurrence of a word of interest, (2) clusters these representations into usage types, and (3) measures change along time.
title: Analysing Lexical Semantic Change with Contextualised Word Representations

subject: unsupervised
source_sentence: We present the first unsupervised approach to lexical semantic change that makes use of state-of-the-art contextualised word representations.
title: Analysing Lexical Semantic Change with Contextualised Word Representations

subject: Contextualised Word Representations
source_sentence: In this work, we investigate the potential of contextualised word representations to detect and analyse lexical seman- tic change , without any lexicographic supervision.
title: Analysing Lexical Semantic Change with Contextualised Word Representations

subject: BERT Language Model
source_sentence: First, given a diachronic corpus and a list of words of interest, we use the BERT language model to compute usage representations for each occurrence of these words.
title: Analysing Lexical Semantic Change with Contextualised Word Representations
section: 3 Method: A Usage-based Approach to Lexical Semantic Change

subject: BERT Language Model
source_sentence: We produce usage representations using the BERT language model , a multi- layer bidirectional Transformer encoder trained on masked token prediction and next sentence predic- tion, on the BooksCorpus (800M words ) and on English text passages extracted from Wikipedia (2,500M words ).
title: Analysing Lexical Semantic Change with Contextualised Word Representations
